paragraphs.source_en: This was because I had always harbored doubts as to whether God, in the matter of manufacturing human beings, was truly great or merely incompetent; but the moment I saw the features of that gentlemanly burglar who appeared so leisurely before me, my doubts were swept away all at once. By features I mean nothing else than this fact: his appearance was the very image of our handsome Mr. Mizushima Kangetsu. Of course I do not have many intimate friends among thieves, but from my usual imaginings of their rough behavior, I had nevertheless formed some notion in my breast of what they must look like. I had decided, quite on my own, that they must have two small round eyes like copper coins and close-cropped bristling heads. But what I actually saw differed from what I had imagined as heaven differs from earth; imagination is not a thing one may let run wild at random. This gentleman burglar was a remarkably stylish and handsome thief. He was tall and slender, slightly dark of complexion, with long, graceful eyebrows. He was perhaps twenty-six or twenty-seven years old, and even in that he was just like Mr. Kangetsu. If God possesses the skill to manufacture two such similar faces, then one certainly cannot call the old gentleman incompetent. No, to tell the truth, his resemblance to Mr. Kangetsu startled me so much that I even wondered whether Kangetsu himself had gone mad and suddenly come out in the middle of the night. Only because this gentleman burglar lacked the faint little tuft of mustache beneath the nose that Kangetsu has did I realize he was not Kangetsu. Mr. Kangetsu is a splendidly handsome man, a handsome man carefully fashioned by God, quite capable of captivating Miss Tomiko, whom Meitei called a living cheque. But judging from the countenance of this gentleman burglar, his attractive force upon Miss Tomiko was in no way inferior to Kangetsu's. If the young lady of the Kaneda household was taken with Mr. Kangetsu's handsome eyes and features, then it would be rather against human feeling were she not to fall for this gentleman burglar with the same ardor. Leaving human feeling aside, it would first of all be illogical. Being so quick-witted and clever as she is, she would surely understand a matter of this sort without anyone having to tell her. It follows, then, that if this gentleman burglar were offered in Kangetsu's stead as her worthy bridegroom, she would surely devote her whole heart to him and enjoy a life of perfect conjugal harmony. Even if, by some chance, Mr. Kangetsu were moved by Meitei's arguments and ruined this match made for all ages; so long as this gentleman burglar remained alive, there would be nothing to fear. Having predicted the future development of events this far, I at last felt reassured on Miss Tomiko's behalf. The existence of this gentleman burglar between heaven and earth is an indispensable condition for Miss Tomiko's happiness in life.

paragraphs.source_zh: 这是因为平时我对神在制造人的问题上到底是伟大还是无能一直有怀疑，而当我看到那位悠然出现的梁上君子面孔的特征时，我的怀疑一下子就打消了。所谓特征不是指别的，而是指这样一个事实：就是说他的模样儿长得和我们的美男子水岛寒月君简直一模一样。我当然不会有很多做小偷的知心朋友，但根据我平时对他们的粗野行为进行的想象，我的胸中也不是没有形成过他们将来的模样。我自以为他们一定有着两只铜钱般的小圆眼睛和短发扎煞着的光头。可是实际看到的和我想象的真有天壤之别，想象这玩意儿可不能随便乱来。这位梁上君子是个很潇洒漂亮的小偷。细高挑儿，肤色微黑，长着秀长的眉毛。年龄大概有二十六七岁吧，就连这点也和寒月君一模一样。神既然有如此手腕制造出两个如此相似的面孔，可见决不能说他老人家无能了。不，说实话，他与寒月君那样的相像着实吓了我一跳，我甚至怀疑是不是寒月君本人神经错乱在半夜突然跑了出来。梁上君子只是没有像寒月君那样在鼻子下长着浅浅的一小撮胡子，这才使我感到他并不是寒月。寒月君是个仪表堂堂的美男子，是个由上帝精心制造出来的美男子，足可以迷住迷亭称之为活支票的富子小姐。但是，从这位梁上君子的尊容来看，他对富子小姐的吸引力比寒月毫不逊色。如果金田家的这位小姐是看中了寒月君俊俏的眉目的话，那么如果她不以同样的热度迷上这位梁上君子就未免太不通人情了。人情还好说，首先不合乎逻辑。你看她是那样的才气横溢而且聪明，不必等人告诉她，这点子事儿她一定会了解的。由此可见，用这位梁上君子来代替寒月做她的乘龙快婿，肯定她会献上全身心的爱，过上琴瑟调和的日子。万一寒月君为迷亭的说法所动，毁了这段千古良缘的话；那么只要这位梁上君子健在，就没什么可怕的，我把事件的未来发展预测到这里，才为富子小姐感到放心。天地间有这位梁上君子的存在，这是富子小姐获得生活幸福必不可少的基本条件。

paragraphs.source_en: The gentleman burglar seemed to be holding something under his arm; when I looked closely, it was the old blanket that my master had just thrown into the study. He wore a checked short coat, had a blue-gray Hakata sash tied above his hips, and from the knees downward his two pale white shins were exposed. He was just lifting one leg to step onto the matting. My master, who for some time had been dreaming that his finger was being caught by a small red-covered book, suddenly rolled over with a thump and shouted, "Kangetsu!" Startled, the gentleman burglar dropped the blanket to the floor and hurriedly drew back the leg he had put forward. One could see the shadows of two long, thin legs reflected on the paper door, trembling faintly. My master groaned and muttered a couple of times, shoved the red book aside, and then, like a man afflicted with ringworm, kept scratching his outstretched black arm with a rasping sound. After that he grew quiet again; his head slipped from the pillow, and he fell into a deep sleep. It appeared that his cry of "Kangetsu" had been nothing more than talk in his sleep. The gentleman burglar stood for a while in the corridor, watching for movement inside the room; once he had made sure that my master and his wife were sound asleep, he again put one leg onto the matting. This time my master's voice calling Kangetsu was no longer heard. Before long he stepped forward with his other leg as well. In the six-mat bedroom, brightly illuminated by a spring lamp, the gentleman burglar's shadow split the room sharply in two, stretching from the wicker trunk past over my head and blackening half the wall. When I turned my head, the shadow of this gentleman burglar was wavering dimly at just about two-thirds of the way up the wall. Though he was a handsome man, if one looked only at his shadow, he was just like a big-headed monster, an exceedingly strange shape. The gentleman burglar looked down at the sleeping face of my master's wife and, for some reason, showed a faint smile. Even the way he smiled was exactly like Kangetsu, and I was greatly astonished.

units.source_en: The gentleman burglar seemed to be holding something under his arm; when I looked closely, it was the old blanket that my master had just thrown into the study.
units.source_zh: 梁上君子在腋下似乎夹着什么，我仔细一看，是刚才主人扔在书斋里的那条旧毛毯。

units.source_en: He wore a checked short coat, had a blue-gray Hakata sash tied above his hips, and from the knees downward his two pale white shins were exposed.
units.source_zh: 他穿着格子布的半截褂，屁股上边系着一条蓝灰色的博多带，从膝头往下露着两条雪白的小腿。

units.source_en: He was just lifting one leg to step onto the matting.
units.source_zh: 他正抬起一条腿迈到席铺上来。

units.source_en: My master, who for some time had been dreaming that his finger was being caught by a small red-covered book, suddenly rolled over with a thump and shouted, "Kangetsu!"
units.source_zh: 主人从刚才起就在做着手指被一本红色封面小书挟住的梦，这时突然来个大翻身，大喊了一声“寒月！”

units.source_en: Startled, the gentleman burglar dropped the blanket to the floor and hurriedly drew back the leg he had put forward.
units.source_zh: 梁上君子一惊之下把毛毯掉在了地上，他急忙将他那迈出的腿缩了回去。

units.source_en: One could see the shadows of two long, thin legs reflected on the paper door, trembling faintly.
units.source_zh: 只见映在纸门上细长的两条腿的黑影在微微抖动。

units.source_en: My master groaned and muttered a couple of times, shoved the red book aside, and then, like a man afflicted with ringworm, kept scratching his outstretched black arm with a rasping sound.

ja.t: はうーん、むにゃむにゃと

units.source_zh: 主人发出两声呃哈呃哈的声音，一下子把那本红皮书捅到一边，然后像害顽癣病一样咔嚓咔嚓不停地搔起他那伸出的黑胳膊。

units.source_en: After that he grew quiet again; his head slipped from the pillow, and he fell into a deep sleep.
units.source_zh: 这以后他又趋于安静，头从枕头上滑了下来，陷入沉睡之中。

units.source_en: It appeared that his cry of "Kangetsu" had been nothing more than talk in his sleep.
units.source_zh: 看来，他喊声“寒月”，完全是梦中的呓语。

units.source_en: The gentleman burglar stood for a while in the corridor, watching for movement inside the room; once he had made sure that my master and his wife were sound asleep, he again put one leg onto the matting.
units.source_zh: 梁上君子在廊子里停了一会儿，窥伺室内的动静，当他看准了主人夫妇都在熟睡，便又向席铺上伸出一条腿。

units.source_en: This time my master's voice calling Kangetsu was no longer heard.
units.source_zh: 这次再也听不见主人叫喊寒月的声音。

units.source_en: Before long he stepped forward with his other leg as well.
units.source_zh: 不一会他又向前迈出了他的另一条腿。

units.source_en: In the six-mat bedroom, brightly illuminated by a spring lamp, the gentleman burglar's shadow split the room sharply in two, stretching from the wicker trunk past over my head and blackening half the wall.
units.source_zh: 这间六叠的卧室里在一盏春灯的灿烂光辉照耀之下，把梁上君子的影子鲜明地分成两个影子，从柳条行李那边一直遮过我的头，黑黑地遮住了半边墙壁。

units.source_en: When I turned my head, the shadow of this gentleman burglar was wavering dimly at just about two-thirds of the way up the wall.
units.source_zh: 我扭头一看，这位梁上君子的黑影正好模模糊糊地映在墙壁的三分之二高度的地方晃来晃去。

units.source_en: Though he was a handsome man, if one looked only at his shadow, he was just like a big-headed monster, an exceedingly strange shape.
units.source_zh: 别看这位是美男子，只看他的影子却活像个大脑袋的怪物，形状奇特得很。

units.source_en: The gentleman burglar looked down at the sleeping face of my master's wife and, for some reason, showed a faint smile.
units.source_zh: 梁上君子俯视了一下主人的妻子熟睡的面孔，不知为什么显出了一丝的笑意。

units.source_en: Even the way he smiled was exactly like Kangetsu, and I was greatly astonished.
units.source_zh: 他连笑法都和寒月一模一样，使我大为吃惊。
